quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Primogem x20, Mora x10000, Strange Part x1

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Ah, you're from the outside. W—Welcome, but... I don't have flowers to give you right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Flowers? Aw, c'mon, there's no need to be so formal.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Oh, okay. In that case, let me just welcome you very, very enthusiastically to Merusea Village. Welcome!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks a lot!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Yup. I'm very enthusiastic, so whatever you want to know, I'll tell you all about it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice! In that case, could you tell us a bit about Merusea Village?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Sure I can. The village is home to lots of Melusines... Well, you can't see them here, but you will if you keep going forward.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Everyone here is a wonderful Melusine, so if you're a good person, you'll definitely be welcomed here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon is too!

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: And that's good to hear!

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: What should I say next? I... forgot... But I remember that the ending was "I hope you enjoy your stay here in our village"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Nice! Shall we go have a look, then, {NICKNAME}? We'll see you later, Cosanzeana!

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: See you. I hope that the next time we meet, I'll have lots of flowers ready for you!

choices.text: I wouldn't say that I've never done any evil...

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: Eh? O—Oh no... I... I have to tell my friends who work at the Marechaussee Phantom...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey, hey, {NICKNAME} was just joking! We haven't done anything worth us being pursued by the Marechaussee Phantom!

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: ...Really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really! Of course really!

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: Okay. I trust you.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Hehe. Being able to show off a flower to humans... Oh, I never even dreamed that such a day might come!

choices.text: As long as your wish can come true.

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: You two are the best! I'll definitely pay back your kindness.

choices.text: Consider it compensation for Paimon's transgressions.

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: Oh, that's fine, I'm already over it! Please, help me bring flowers from other lands so I can build the most beautiful garden!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Windwheel Asters, for example.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right. Windwheel Asters grow out in the wild, and they're a tough breed. Maybe they'll also grow here!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: "Pinwheel Asters"... I've never heard that name before. Are they really spikey or something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, not really. "Windwheels" are things you put on buildings. They have big sails that are like flower petals, and when the wind blows, they spin like this — fwoop, fwoop, fwoop!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Windwheel Asters are called that because they spin in the wind as well.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: So they spin and make fwoop noises? Amazing! I wish I could go see them right now!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I think that'll do for now.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, since you're so curious, Cosanzeana, why don't we help you look for a few exotic flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: You really would? In that case, could I have all of them at— Wait... no, no. I have to be a responsible florist, so just one type will do for starters.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... What kind of flowers would you be willing to bring me?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Distant land's flowers, flowers from a distant land~ now I have you in my hand!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Can you think of any other suitable flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Distant land's flowers, flowers from a distant land~ now I have you in my hand!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Distant land's flowers, flowers from a distant land~ now I have you in my hand!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go with a Windwheel Aster.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, sure! This isn't something you see often in Fontaine, so it'll make for awesome bragging rights with the humans here!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Distant land's flowers, flowers from a distant land~ now I have you in my hand!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's get her a Silk Flower.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, sure! This isn't something you see often in Fontaine, so it'll make for awesome bragging rights with the humans here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew! Planting these flowers is pretty tough!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You say that, but it was Cosanzeana and I who did the work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's been super concerned for these flowers, you know! Mental stress counts as work too!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Flowers from distant lands... So strange, yet so beautiful. Hehe, my flower garden will be the envy of the humans!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, you don't see them in Fontaine often, so make sure to show them off to the people here a little more, hehe!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't think that you would see flowers so differently from us, Cosanzeana... and that explaining things would be so tough... Paimon's head hurts now.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Why would your head hurt? You think that those flowers are beautiful, and I see them exactly the same way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, they are pretty, but Paimon wouldn't call our perspectives "exactly the same." We definitely share an appreciation for flowers, though, so there's no need to sweat the small stuff — you just concentrate on taking care of them!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Yes! Next, I must find some <color=#00E1FFFF>water</color> with which to nourish my precious flowers...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No need to trouble yourself, I'll fetch some for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That's right, just leave it to {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Naku Weeds, for example.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, that's a good idea! Naku Weeds can even grow in places that are stormy all year round. Surely Merusea Village doesn't have weather that bad!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Not-Cool Weeds? A strange name. I've heard that humans display flowers at their "horticultural fairs." Do humans abroad display weeds, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, no. Naku Weeds are a type of flower, not a weed. Even if the wind isn't blowing, they will gently shake when thunder can be heard. That's why the locals use them to predict the coming of a storm!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Flowers that can vibrate by themselves... I wonder what those might look like. I'd really want to see them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That should do it. Now we just need to leave the flowers to grow.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I hope your garden blooms and prospers.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Oh, flowers from a distant land... I promise I will cherish you and care for you.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: The two of you have given me such exotic flowers, and I too must repay you with things that are every bit as beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh, c'mon, you're making Paimon blush... But, um, is this component the "thing as beautiful as a flower"?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: That's right! These components are both lovely and useful to the village, which is why I love them, and love collecting them! I look at them every day, and they make me very happy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Uh, you could call components "useful," but "beautiful"...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Y'know, Paimon, you find Mora beautiful.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Hehe, that's true. And looking at Mora every day does make Paimon super happy...)

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: "Human lives are so hard," I thought, "so what do they see that makes them happy?" So I went to the human village, and there I saw all the beautiful flowers they had!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: If Merusea Village were to be filled with all those lovely flowers, I am sure everyone would be very happy.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: That's why I've decided to become a florist, one who will plant a lovely flower garden in our village! I will succeed, even if it means that I must give up some of my beautiful components and work as hard as humans do...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow. Paimon didn't realize how much you're willing to do for the flowers you love so much... Your sacrifices won't be in vain! Paimon, kind soul that she is, will continue helping you for sure!

choices.text: You could totally learn from her, you know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, uh... Because Paimon's got you, the super kind-hearted {NICKNAME} around, Paimon only needs to do a liiittle bit of work!

choices.text: ...And make that Mora you love so much yourself...

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Why? Why won't they sprout...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, what are you busy with? Ooh. This is what they call a "home vegetable garden," right?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: A v—vegetable garden? But this is supposed to be a flower garden... Oh no, I'm not a very good florist, am I...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Did Paimon get something wrong? Sorry, sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so was this what you were talking about previously when you said that you had no flowers to give us, Cosanzeana?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: That's right. I've planted all these seeds, but nothing's happened yet. They aren't all ruined, are they?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That would be such a shame! You'd need to start over in that case, wouldn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: That's right. I mean, what I want is a beautiful flower garden... I don't want people to call it a vegetable garden...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm. If that's the case, just let us, the ever-helpful helpers, help you!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: #Paimon and {NICKNAME}... Do you know how to garden? Can you help me?

choices.text: I've been known to plant some flowers and crops here and there.

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: Ooh, that's so cool! My wish is to become an awesome florist! ...But the flowers I plant always wither.

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: I tried transplanting flowers at first, but they always died. After that, I tried to start them off from seeds, but they just refuse to sprout...

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: Flowers are so beautiful, but raising them is so hard... But humans have gotten used to such hard work, so they have an easy time caring for flowers.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe humans just plant flowers in environments better suited to growing them.

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: The environment... The humans who sell flowers also said that "flowers grow better outside." But if I do that, it'll be hard for me to go care for them.

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: It is said that there are all sorts of flowers in faraway places, and maybe, just maybe, some of them might do better here in the village... But I can't go so far from home to collect them myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hehe, then you've met the right people! We, Paimon and {NICKNAME}, have traveled everywhere, and we've seen all sorts of flowers!

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: Humans learn by watching others so easily. I tried doing that too, but I still keep failing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Silk Flowers, for example.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Silt Flowers? What a strange name. Do they grow in the muck and mud?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, that's not it! If you hear "silk," it means pretty clothes! The flowers themselves are beautiful too, and they can even be worn!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Pretty flowers from another land that you can wear? ... That's so cool. I wish I could see one right now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sumeru Roses, for instance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, you can find Sumeru Roses everywhere in Sumeru's rainforests. It's a really tough plant! The rainforest is also pretty humid, so it's quite similar to Merusea Village.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Sumeru Roses... I've tried planting other roses. Is there any difference between them and the ones from Sumeru?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Y'know, Paimon doesn't really know all that much about flower varieties, but its color, at least, is definitely different from the ones you find in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But the Sumeru Rose's most distinguishing feature is its scent! You can use it to make great perfumes, and it's amazing when added to desserts, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: I've never seen such an exotic rose before, and with a special scent, you say... Mm, I'd love to get a whiff of that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Odds are that Paimon will eat it before you get a chance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Paimon won't do that! She'll at least wait till it's been made into a proper dish first!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's give her a Naku Weed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, sure! This isn't something you see often in Fontaine, so it'll make for awesome bragging rights with the humans here!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's find her a Sumeru Rose.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, sure! This isn't something you see often in Fontaine, so it'll make for awesome bragging rights with the humans here!

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Ah, so Windwheel Asters are these golden-red flowers. They're so warm and bright.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: And they really do spin, just like you said, Paimon! Ooh, it does burn the eyes a tad to stare too long at them, though.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Golden... and eye-scorching?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Since Windwheel Asters are so bright, the "windwheels" themselves must be really bright, too. People must mount them on their homes to produce light, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, that's not how we use them, no.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Ah, so Silk Flowers are these crystal-clear things. They look so much like pearls!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh, really? Are they?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: If one were to wear these flowers, it would be like wearing a waterfall! I've never seen such clothes before, though.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Neither has Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Hmm, yes! This must be what the humans call "fashion" — the stranger the better, so I hear.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, that's not how you use Silk Flowers, and that's not what fashion is either... is it?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: So these are the vibrating flowers...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Without thunder all around and in a cave like this, you can barely tell that they're moving.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: ...It's hard to make out, but the sound they make when vibrating is very beautiful!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They make beautiful sounds? Paimon can't hear 'em, though...

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: The sound is crisp and pleasant to the ear — ah, I can't get enough of it! Such lovely flowers, that sing with such lovely voices...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. It seems she really can hear the sound of a Naku Weed when it vibrates. Look how engrossed she is...

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Hmm... If this "thunder" thing strikes, the Naku Weeds will vibrate more strongly, and the sound they make will be louder, right?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Hmmm... This must be because all flowers need fertilizer, and "thunder" is that of the Naku Weed... Do you know where we might buy this "thunder"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: From the Raiden Shogun? ...Wait, but thunder isn't fertilizer in the first place!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehehe, you can't smell those Sumeru Roses without being reminded of the delicious dishes you can make using them! Rose Custard, Candied Ajilenakh Nuts, Lambad Fish Roll...

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: So this is the Sumeru Rose that you love to eat, Paimon... So many petals, with so many colors...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Sumeru Roses... have many colors?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: That's right. Petals of many colors combine to form this flower, and their colors shift as it rocks back and forth...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They... even change color?

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Now I get it! When you put Sumeru Roses into food, the food itself will also start to turn into a rainbow of shifting colors. No wonder you love those dishes, Paimon — they must be truly beautiful!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon thinks that you'd only see multicolored food that changes color after eating some poisonous mushrooms...

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Flowers from a distant land, a distant land's flowers~ Have you two brought some today? Is this the hour?

choices.text: (Give Cosanzeana some exotic flowers to try growing.)

response.speaker: Cosanzeana
response.text: #Oh, I don't mean to be a bother... but could you be faster, {NICKNAME}, just a little faster? They're all I can think about now...

response.text: #Oh, I don't mean to be a bother... but could you be faster, {NICKNAME}, just a little faster? They're all I can think about now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #If you've made your decision, {NICKNAME}, let's give those flowers to Cosanzeana.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #If you've made your decision, {NICKNAME}, let's give those flowers to Cosanzeana.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #If you've made your decision, {NICKNAME}, let's give those flowers to Cosanzeana.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #If you've made your decision, {NICKNAME}, let's give those flowers to Cosanzeana.

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: Ah, little flowers, you've come from so far away. You must be thirsty! Come, have some water, so you can grow...

dialogues.speaker: Cosanzeana
dialogues.text: I thought some baddie was going to ruin my flower garden again, but it seems like things are fine. What a relief...
